lessons.title: Upstream ctor switching from module-global to class-attribute hooks silently breaks ascend monkeypatch-swap subclasses
lessons.symptom: Ascend model subclass (e.g. vllm_ascend/models/qwen3_dflash2.py) activates its behavior by swapping a module global in the upstream parent's module during __init__; after an upstream refactor the draft model silently builds the wrong layers/selector (missing weights, degraded dflash2→dflash1) without any error.
lessons.root_cause: The ascend model activated its subclass behavior by temporarily rebinding module globals (dflash_mod.DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer / DFlashQwen3Model). Upstream refactored the ctors to read self.decoder_layer_cls / self.model_cls class attributes, so the rebinding no longer affects construction: plain DFlash1 layers are built (missing attention_conv/mlp_conv/candidate_selector weights) with no import error — pure silent degradation.
fix_guidance: When an upstream __init__ stops reading a module global, set the matching class attribute on the ascend subclass — it is inert on older pins where the parent still reads the global
Keep the module-global swap when the release pin (e.g. 0.27.1) predates the hook; it becomes inert on main, no vllm_version_is guard needed
Grep vllm_ascend/models for the same swap pattern (X = Y assignments to imported upstream modules) before declaring the fix complete

Note: ModelRegistry.register_model does dict assignment, so ascend plugin registrations overwrite upstream entries for the same arch name — duplicate registration of DFlash2DraftModel is not a conflict
lessons.example: step-1 @ vllm 27ec8ac6: upstream qwen3_dflash.py added decoder_layer_cls/model_cls (PR 52816); vllm_ascend/models/qwen3_dflash2.py swap hack went dead, fixed by adding decoder_layer_cls = DFlash2Qwen3DecoderLayer and model_cls = DFlash2Qwen3Model to the ascend subclasses while keeping the swap for the 0.27.1 pin.

lessons.title: Module-level patch().start() mocks die mid-batch when another UT file calls mock.patch.stopall() — re-arm in setUpClass
keywords: pipeline model parallel group is not initialized
lessons.symptom: UTs that construct objects calling distributed-group getters (get_pp_group/get_tp_group/...) fail with "pipeline model parallel group is not initialized" only in the shared-process batch (or intermittently by file order), while passing standalone.
lessons.root_cause: Module-level patch(...).start() mocks in one test file are global to the shared pytest process; any other file calling mock.patch.stopall() (e.g. to clean leaked patches) deactivates them, so tests that depend on those mocks fail only when batch execution order puts them after the stopall — order-dependent flakiness that does not reproduce when the file runs alone.
fix_guidance: Add a rearm helper that re-starts the same patches, and call it from setUpClass of every class whose tests depend on the mocks — setUpClass runs immediately before the class's tests, so no interleaved stopall can intervene
Do NOT call stop() in cleanup for re-armed patchers: after a foreign stopall() already stopped them, stop() raises RuntimeError; leaking them matches the file's existing module-level patch style
Source-side defensive getattr is the wrong fix when the invariant (initialized distributed groups) genuinely holds in production — fix the test's assumptions instead
Verify statically by grepping the attribute-access chain: the traceback frame naming the call site tells you which module namespace must hold the mock
lessons.example: step-1 fix round: tests/ut/kv_offload/test_mooncake_connector.py relied on module-level patch().start() for get_pp_group/get_pcp_group mocks; test_utils.py's test_enable_sp_uses_upstream_parallel_config calls mock.patch.stopall() mid-batch, so 5 thread-constructing tests failed with "pipeline model parallel group is not initialized". Fixed by rearm_group_patches() called in setUpClass of the three thread-constructing classes (no stop() — avoids double-stop RuntimeError after foreign stopall).
